section: Introduction > An emerging fire frontier in temperate mountains

section: Introduction > An emerging fire frontier in temperate mountains
source_says: Intro cites C3S/WMO: European BA and emissions reached record levels in 2025, largest contributions from Iberia. Own MODIS analysis: continental BA below average; EFFIS shows record 19,629 km2.
issue: Record is a secondary statement (C3S/WMO) and conflicts with Burton's own MODIS finding of below-average continental BA; record holds for EFFIS and the Mediterranean biome.
proposed_fix: Say 'by EFFIS accounting, burnt area in Europe reached a record in 2025, concentrated in Iberia'; note the preprint status.

section: Introduction > An emerging fire frontier in temperate mountains

section: Introduction > Why mountain fire is a distinct problem
source_says: One Tasmanian fire (Riveaux Road 2019), 3 isochrones: conducive structures 6.5% to 40% with ruggedness; surface-wind (WindNinja) runs worse in rugged terrain.
issue: Generalised from one fire and three isochrones; experiment-group skill also fell with ruggedness. Imported (Australia).
proposed_fix: Add 'in one Tasmanian fire' and mark as non-European evidence.

section: Introduction > Why mountain fire is a distinct problem
source_says: Upper winds over rugged terrain give variable, turbulent, discontinuous conditions; the assumed fire-weather continuum has reduced validity in mountains.

section: Introduction > Why mountain fire is a distinct problem
source_says: Median 3-D length of steepest upslope paths within forest, per each of 21 Swiss pyroregions, explains R2 0.558-0.651 of large-fire statistics; no weather variable used.
issue: One combined metric (path length within forest), regressed across 21 pyroregion medians; method assumes extreme fire weather.

section: Introduction > Why mountain fire is a distinct problem

section: Introduction > Why mountain fire is a distinct problem

section: Introduction > Why mountain fire is a distinct problem

section: Conclusions
source_says: States land abandonment is underrepresented in continental analyses; warming raises fuel cover above 1,400 m. No finding that abandonment created continuous fuel on steep slopes.
issue: Beloiu does not support the abandonment/steep-slope fuel claim. The preceding uncited 72 m/decade sentence is Beloiu's.
proposed_fix: Move Beloiu to the 72 m/decade sentence; keep Conedera/Gerberding for the fuel-bed claim.

section: Conclusions
source_says: Abandonment turned marginal land into forest/fallow; continuous forest on long slopes raises large-fire propensity.
issue: Swiss case; abandonment point is secondary (Gellrich et al.).

section: Conclusions
source_says: Mentions abandonment leading to encroachment, connectivity and fuel build-up (citing Bebi, Tasser, Valese).
issue: Secondary mention, not a result; nothing on steep slopes or large-fire development.
proposed_fix: Rely on Conedera 2024 / Bebi for the steep-slope fuel claim; keep Gerberding for the projected rise.

section: Conclusions
source_says: ~80% of fires <1 ha; most Alpine forest species not fire-adapted (e.g. beech).

section: Conclusions
source_says: Dominant Central European species (fir, spruce, beech) have low bark fire resistance.
issue: Species-level bark data, not stand tolerance.

section: Conclusions
source_says: Mean fire size ~9 ha; Alpine vegetation generally considered sensitive to fire.
issue: Valese supports fire-sensitive vegetation but does not state that most fires are <1 ha (that is Müller).
proposed_fix: Keep Valese only for fire-sensitive stands.

section: Conclusions
source_says: Same as above: one case; protective value high; timber value not computed (negative stumpage of interventions).
issue: "Worth more as protection than as timber" not directly shown; single case.
proposed_fix: Soften to "in the cases valued, protective value is high and protective silviculture is unprofitable".

section: Conclusions
source_says: Root reinforcement and protective capacity lost within ~15 years, not recovering for decades.

section: Conclusions
source_says: Mentions partial vegetation regrowth and catchment recovery capacity in susceptibility mapping; no analysis of threshold recovery over time.
issue: La Porta does not show the threshold recovering as vegetation returns; only Rengers (Colorado) supports this.
proposed_fix: Cite Rengers alone and say 'Evidence from Colorado suggests...'.

section: Conclusions
source_says: Monetised protective effect; no timber value.
issue: No protection-vs-timber comparison in Moos.
proposed_fix: Cite Moos only for protection value or remove from the comparison.

section: Conclusions
source_says: No debris flows in year 2 despite exceedances, attributed to vegetation recovery and sediment depletion.
issue: 'Duration matters more than initial drop' is the review's inference.
